name: Level-order Linewise
html:
Welcome back, dear reader. So, how is it going with the generic trees? We hope that you have solved the previous problem Level Order Of A Generic Tree . If you have not solved this problem, we recommend you solve it first as it is the basis for this problem. You can also refer to LEVEL ORDER OF A GENERIC TREE-SOLUTION VIDEO to understand what is level order and how do we print the level order of a generic tree. So, this question is called LEVEL ORDER-LINE WISE.

Important Links : Problem Link, Question Video, Solution Video

Problem Discussion :

We have to print the level order of a generic tree line wise i.e. all the elements which belong to the same level should be printed in one line and the elements of the next levels should be printed in the next line. This is shown in the example shown below:

You may refer to the question video if you have any doubts regarding the question.

Watch video Approach :

Let us start our discussion about the procedure directly without wasting any time. Have a look at the diagram shown below: (fig-2)

Initial Condition: We are currently at the root node and we have inserted the root node into the queue.

Printing-Level-Order: Now we will start our "Remove-Print-Add" algorithm. So, we will remove the data from the main queue (you know that removal will take place from the front of the queue only) and print the data and then push all its children into the child queue.

Now, before removing the value from the main queue we check whether it has some values in it or not. Since we find that the main queue is empty, we will leave a line (in the console i.e. hit enter or print " ") and copy all the elements of the child queue to the main queue and empty the child queue.

This is shown in the figure below (fig-4).

So, whenever the main queue becomes empty, we will leave a line and we will copy all the elements of the child queue to the main queue and make the child queue empty.

So, we have completed one level. Whenever the main queue becomes empty, we complete a level.

Now again, let's repeat our algorithm "Remove-Print-Add". We remove 20 from the queue and print it and add its children 50 and 60 to the child node.

In the next step, we again perform our algorithm. We will remove 30 from the queue, print it and add all its children to the child queue.

Now, we will remove 40, print it and add its children to the child queue.

Now, when we try to remove an element, we find that the main queue has become empty. So, we will leave a line, and copy all the elements of the child queue to the main queue and the main queue will become empty.

Now, we will again continue with our algorithm "Remove-Print-Add". So, remove 50 from the queue, print it and add its child nodes to the child queue. Since 50 does not have any child nodes, nothing will be added to the child queue.

Now, remove 60 from the queue, print it and add its child nodes to the child queue. Since 60 does not have any child nodes, nothing will be added to the child queue.

Similarly, remove 70 from the queue, print it and add its child nodes to the child queue. Since 70 does not have any child nodes, nothing will be added to the child queue.

Similarly, remove 80 from the queue, print it and add its child nodes to the child queue. So, 110 and 120 will be added to the child queue.

Similarly we will remove 90 and 100. Since both of them do not have any child nodes, nothing will be added to the child queue and 90 and 100 will be printed.

Now, when we try to remove an element from the main queue, it is already empty. So, we will leave a line and copy all the elements of the child queue to the main queue and empty the child queue.

Now only two nodes are left in the main queue. Both of them do not have any child nodes. So, we will remove them from the queue, print them and the child queue will remain empty (see fig-15).

Notice that both the queues are empty now. This has never happened in any step before this step. When both the queues are empty it means that we have completed all the levels of the tree. So, we can stop our procedure when both the main queue and the child queue become empty.

So, dear reader, did you get this procedure? The first step of inserting the root node into the main queue was unique. Rest all the steps are repetitive. We are performing the same algorithm of "Remove-Print-Add" again and again and whenever the main queue becomes empty, we copy the contents of the child queue to the main queue, empty the child queue and continue our procedure. If you still have any doubts regarding the above procedure, you may refer to the solution video to clear all your doubts. Now that we have understood the entire procedure, let us write the code.

Watch video Algorithm:
  1. Take 2 queues. One is called the main queue and the other is called the child queue. We will use the same "Remove-Print-Add" algorithm that we learnt in the previous question. We will start from the root node and print it and remove it from the queue (as it is initially kept in the main queue).
  2. Then we will add all the children of this node into the child queue and repeat the "Remove-Print-Add" algorithm until both the main queue and the child queue become empty.
  3. Also, in between the procedure, whenever the main queue becomes empty we will leave a line and we will copy all the contents of the child queue to the main queue and the child queue becomes empty. So, this is the algorithm that we are going to follow.
import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { private static class Node { int data; ArrayList< Node> children = new ArrayList< >(); } public static void display(Node node) { String str = node.data + " -> "; for (Node child : node.children) { str += child.data + ", "; } str += "."; System.out.println(str); for (Node child : node.children) { display(child); } } public static Node construct(int[] arr) { Node root = null; Stack< Node> st = new Stack< >(); for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { if (arr[i] == -1) { st.pop(); } else { Node t = new Node(); t.data = arr[i]; if (st.size() > 0) { st.peek().children.add(t); } else { root = t; } st.push(t); } } return root; } public static int size(Node node) { int s = 0; for (Node child : node.children) { s += size(child); } s += 1; return s; } public static int max(Node node) { int m = Integer.MIN_VALUE; for (Node child : node.children) { int cm = max(child); m = Math.max(m, cm); } m = Math.max(m, node.data); return m; } public static int height(Node node) { int h = -1; for (Node child : node.children) { int ch = height(child); h = Math.max(h, ch); } h += 1; return h; } public static void traversals(Node node){ System.out.println("Node Pre " + node.data); for(Node child: node.children){ System.out.println("Edge Pre " + node.data + "--" + child.data); traversals(child); System.out.println("Edge Post " + node.data + "--" + child.data); } System.out.println("Node Post " + node.data); } public static void levelOrderLinewise(Node node){ Queue< Node> queue = new ArrayDeque< >(); queue.add(node); Queue< Node> cqueue = new ArrayDeque< >(); while(queue.size() > 0){ node = queue.remove(); System.out.print(node.data + " "); for(Node child: node.children){ cqueue.add(child); } if(queue.size() == 0){ queue = cqueue; cqueue = new ArrayDeque< >(); System.out.println(); } } } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); int[] arr = new int[n]; String[] values = br.readLine().split(" "); for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { arr[i] = Integer.parseInt(values[i]); } Node root = construct(arr); levelOrderLinewise(root); } }
java; true";

So, dear reader, did you understand the above code? If you have any doubts regarding the above code, you may refer to the solution video (2:24 onwards) to understand the code completely and clear your doubts. Now let us discuss the time and space complexity.

Watch video Analysis: Time Complexity:

O(n)

The time complexity of the above code is O(n) as we are traversing all the nodes of the generic tree once to print them.

Space Complexity:

O(n)

The space complexity of the above code is O(n) as we are storing every node in one or the other queue.

We hope that you understood everything including the time and space complexity. Still if you have any doubts, refer to the complete solution video and all your doubts will be cleared.

Watch video Suggestions:

Here are some suggestions from our side that you do not want to miss:

  1. If you have come to this problem directly and are now having doubts about what exactly a level order traversal is, we recommend you solve the previous problem LEVEL ORDER OF A GENERIC TREE.
  2. We recommend you do this hard work of drawing both the queues and their situation for every node as this will give you a great insight. Till then, Happy Coding!!!
